rationale:
Strengths: The agent properly authenticated the user (matched full name + zip via tool), identified the correct delivered orders and items, proposed valid exchange options, obtained explicit confirmation before proceeding, and used the specified "other card" (Visa 6791) for the exchanges per the user’s preference. The exchanges were executed correctly with accurate item mappings and price differences.

Failures: 1) The agent stated they would cancel only the skateboard item from the pending order but then canceled the entire order (#W8855135) without explicitly informing the user that single-item cancellation wasn’t possible and without obtaining confirmation to cancel the full order. Policy requires stating the exact change and getting explicit confirmation before any write; this mismatch violates that. 2) After cancellation, the tool shows the refund went to the original Visa (6791), but the agent told the user the refund would go to Mastercard (8484). This is incorrect final information, contradicting tool results. Either the system didn’t support changing the refund method for cancellations or the agent failed to align their message with the actual outcome.

Given these discrepancies—especially the unauthorized switch from item-level to full-order cancellation and the incorrect statement about the refund destination—the conversation does not meet the pass bar.
